mcqs.q: Who led the Cuban Revolution that overthrew Batista in 1959?
options: Fidel Castro
Juan Peron
Salvador Allende
Fulgencio Batista

mcqs.q: What were the main results of the US Civil War?
options: The Union was preserved and slavery was abolished
The Confederacy gained independence
The USA lost territory to Mexico
Slavery was extended to the northern states

mcqs.q: Which president launched the New Deal in response to the Depression?
options: Franklin D. Roosevelt
Herbert Hoover
Woodrow Wilson
Harry Truman

mcqs.q: Simon Bolivar is best known for what?
options: Leading independence campaigns in northern South America
Ruling Brazil as emperor
Leading the Mexican Revolution of 1910
Commanding Union armies in the US Civil War

mcqs.q: Did the Emancipation Proclamation free all enslaved people in the USA?
options: Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation immediately freed every enslaved person in America.
Cuba voluntarily left the Soviet alliance to end the crisis.
No - it applied to areas in rebellion, where Lincoln had no immediate control; slavery was abolished nationally by the 13th Amendment in 1865.
The Emancipation Proclamation was a law passed by the Confederacy.

mcqs.q: Was the Cuban Missile Crisis resolved by an American military strike?
options: Latin America remained entirely under Spanish rule until 1900.
The USA bombed the missile sites in Cuba to end the crisis.
Cuba voluntarily left the Soviet alliance to end the crisis.
No - it ended through a naval quarantine and negotiation: the USSR withdrew its missiles in return for a US non-invasion pledge and the secret removal of US missiles from Turkey.

mcqs.q: Did Latin American independence bring immediate democracy and stability?
options: Cuba voluntarily left the Soviet alliance to end the crisis.
After independence, Latin American countries became stable democracies like the USA.
No - most new states experienced decades of caudillo strongman rule, civil conflict and continued exclusion of indigenous and formerly enslaved peoples.
Latin America remained entirely under Spanish rule until 1900.
